slides.title: A shared rooftop array could undercut what blocks C and D pay for daytime power

lines.text: We propose a 12-month pilot on two roofs.

notes.heading: A synthetic brief
notes.text: Larkmoor Housing Co-op, its residents, every figure and every source in this deck are invented for a test brief. None of it describes a real co-op or a real installation. Larkmoor Co-op energy audit 2025 (synthetic)

notes.heading: What the pilot is
notes.text: One array on each south-facing roof, blocks C and D: 64 kW in all, quoted at £86,400 installed, including scaffolding and a five-year service plan. Installer quotation Q-2291

slides.title: About 40% of what flats on blocks C and D spend on electricity falls in daylight hours

lines.text: median yearly electricity spend per flat, 2025

notes.heading: Median of the bills residents shared
notes.text: The audit covers the 48 flats on blocks C and D; 41 households shared their 2025 bills. The median annual spend was £612 per flat. Larkmoor Co-op energy audit 2025, p4

notes.heading: Daylight hours
notes.text: The audit counts spend between 08:00 and 18:00 as daylight: about 40% of the total. That is the share a rooftop array can supply directly. Larkmoor Co-op energy audit 2025, p6

slides.title: 26 of the 33 households that answered the survey support a pilot

lines.text: We sit under that roof all day and still pay peak rates for the lights.
Blocks C and D resident survey, Sep 2026

notes.heading: Who answered
notes.text: 33 of the 48 households on blocks C and D answered; 26 support a pilot. That is 79% of respondents and 54% of all households. Fifteen households did not reply. Blocks C and D resident survey, Sep 2026, Q3

slides.title: A 12-month pilot tests savings and upkeep on two roofs first

notes.heading: What the quote covers
notes.text: 64 kW across both roofs for £86,400 installed, including scaffolding and a five-year service plan. Blocks A and B have no quote yet, so they are out of scope until the review. Installer quotation Q-2291

notes.heading: What the review decides
notes.text: After twelve months the board sees measured savings and upkeep and decides whether to extend the scheme to other blocks or stop. Installer quotation Q-2291, §5

notes.heading: One array per roof
notes.text: Each roof’s array feeds that block’s landlord supply, which runs the shared parts of the building and offsets daytime power bought from the grid. Installer quotation Q-2291, §2

notes.heading: How a flat sees the saving
notes.text: Flats see a monthly credit, split pro rata to each flat’s daytime use. Installer quotation Q-2291, §2

notes.heading: Upkeep
notes.text: One inspection and panel clean a year. The five-year service plan covers it; afterwards it costs £1,150 a year for both roofs. Installer quotation Q-2291, §5

slides.title: Roof leaks, falling tariffs and later upkeep are the pilot’s main risks

lines.text: Upkeep after year five: £1,150 a year
Adds inverter replacement and 2% yearly output loss

notes.heading: Residents’ main worry
notes.text: Nine survey respondents named roof leaks during installation as their main worry. Blocks C and D resident survey, Sep 2026, Q5

sources.text: Blocks C and D resident survey, Sep 2026, Q5

notes.heading: Single-sourced forecast
notes.text: Single-sourced: one regional tariff forecast says prices may fall next year, which would shrink the saving. No second source supports or contradicts it. Regional energy outlook, Oct 2026

notes.heading: Upkeep after the plan
notes.text: One inspection and panel clean a year costs £1,150 for both roofs once the five-year service plan ends. Installer quotation Q-2291, §5

notes.heading: Disputed payback
notes.text: Disputed: the installer puts payback at about 7 years at current tariffs (relayed in the quote). The treasurer puts it at about 11 years once inverter replacement and a 2% yearly output loss are counted. The deck shows both. Installer quotation Q-2291, §6 Treasurer’s note to the board, 14 Oct 2026
